# 9. The finite-bit compiler and the actual constants \(A,p\)

It remains to distinguish numerical bounds from representation bounds.

## 9.1 Numerical bounds depend only on \(R\)

The choices are triangular:
\[
(q,K_0,a)
\longrightarrow\Gamma
\longrightarrow T
\longrightarrow\mathcal J
\longrightarrow r
\longrightarrow r_0
\longrightarrow\beta
\longrightarrow h
\longrightarrow\sigma
\longrightarrow e
\longrightarrow\delta.
\]
Every reciprocal is bounded by a fixed polynomial in \(R\).

For example,
\[
\beta^{-1}
\le1000+10^6\Gamma^8\rho^{-1}T^{-1},
\]
\[
h^{-1}
\le
1000T^{-1}
+10^6\Gamma^8\rho^{-1}T^{-2}
+\left(10^6\Gamma^8K_0^2r^{-1}\right)^8,
\]
and
\[
\delta^{-1}
\le
100(\beta h)^{-1}
+c_*^{-1}\mu^{-3}r^{-4}e^{-4}K_\star^{12}.
\]

A degree ledger makes this dependence explicit. If
\[
a\lesssim X^{A_0},\quad q^{-1}\lesssim X^{Q_0},\quad
K_0\lesssim X^{B_0},\quad\Gamma\lesssim X^\gamma,
\]
one may use
\[
\begin{aligned}
t&=\max(1,\gamma,2A_0),&
j&=\gamma+2t,\\
d_r&=\gamma+j+B_0+Q_0,&
d_{r_0}&=d_r+2\gamma,\\
d_\beta&=8\gamma+1+t,\\
d_h&=\max\{t,\,8\gamma+1+2t,\,
                 8(d_r+8\gamma+2B_0)\},\\
d_\sigma&=\max\{d_\beta+d_h,\,
                 7+8d_{r_0}+20(\gamma+B_0)\},\\
d_e&=1+d_{r_0}+d_\sigma,\\
d_\delta&=\max\{d_\beta+d_h,\,
                 3+4d_r+4d_e+12(\gamma+B_0)\}.
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{9.1}
\]
These bound the respective inverse parameters. Here one can take \(A_0=13\), \(Q_0=10\), \(B_0=1\).

Apply the accepted fixed erasing-word bounds to these envelopes, multiply by the polynomial macro and microcycle counts, compose the fixed lowering bound \(D_*\) times, and add the depth-two writer bound. This produces a polynomial numerical envelope
\[
E_{\rm phys}(R)
\]
for force peak and \(\eta^{-1}\).

Since \(\tau\le1\),
\[
\int_0^\tau\|f(t)\|_{W^{1,\infty}}\,dt
\le\sup_t\|f(t)\|_{W^{1,\infty}}.
\]

The only lowering of the enlarged eraser uses a **fixed** catalogue. Variable target synthesis uses the supplied fixed-depth writer. Neither exponent depends on the variable Fourier radius.

## 9.2 Rational heights are bounded separately

The implementation uses the following rules.

- Parameter formulas have fixed algebraic depth.
- Repeated words reuse stored parameters.
- Repeated knots are computed from integer indices and stored rational lengths.
- Target modes are coalesced before numerical coeff

# 1. Notation and the fixed effective constants

Write
\[
\mathcal B(v,w)=P[(v\cdot\nabla)w],\qquad
C_vw=(v\cdot\nabla)w-(w\cdot\nabla)v,
\]
and
\[
L_vw=\mathcal B(v,w)+\mathcal B(w,v).
\]
Set
\[
\mu=\min(\nu,\rho),\qquad \kappa=2\pi.
\]

Use the Fourier Sobolev norms associated with \(I-\Delta\), and put
\[
\|(v,b)\|_{\mathcal H^s}
=\bigl(\|v\|_{H^s}^2+\|b\|_{H^s}^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
\]

Two elementary estimates used repeatedly are
\[
\|\mathcal B(v,w)\|_{H^{-3/4}}
+\|C_vw\|_{H^{-3/4}}
\le C\|v\|_{H^1}\|w\|_{H^1},                                      \tag{1.1}
\]
and
\[
\|\mathcal B(v,w)\|_2+\|C_vw\|_2
\le C\|(v,w)\|_{\mathcal H^1}^{3/2}
       \|(v,w)\|_{\mathcal H^2}^{1/2}.                            \tag{1.2}
\]
The second estimate, rather than (1.1), is used in \(H^1\) energy inequalities.

These constants can be bounded rationally without a norm oracle. For example, dyadic Fourier-shell estimates give the required Agmon inequality and strict Sobolev embeddings. All subsequent derivative orders are fixed.

## Fixed precomputation

Fix the enlarged erasing family and erasing word supplied by the accepted NS construction. Adjoin the twelve fundamental fields. Fix its finite signed Fourier lowering table to the twelve fields, of depth \(D_*\).

Precompute estimates through \(H^{12}\), including signed operator scales
\[
H^{s+2}\longrightarrow H^s,\qquad -8\le s\le8.
\]
Only a smaller range is ultimately necessary, but this choice avoids endpoint bookkeeping issues.

The precomputation produces:

- the fixed Fourier tables and rational saturation certificates;
- the supplied word constants and polynomial resource bounds;
- fixed-order bounds for the Euler and induction propagators;
- rational constants in the product, energy, commutator and parabolic estimates below.

Here is a concrete bounding procedure for these constants. For each fixed Fourier field \(F\), form weighted coefficient sums such as
\[
b_j(F)=
1+\sum_{k}
 (1+7|k|_1)^{j+4}
 \bigl(|a_k|_1+|b_k|_1\bigr).
\]
Differentiate finite Fourier expressions explicitly; bound products by products of weighted coefficient sums; use \(\kappa<7\), \(\|P\|_{H^s\to H^s}\le1\), and rational versions of Young’s inequality.
